Incorporating the latest Beige Book color tempers the FOMC’s “solid pace” characterization. Across districts such as Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, and Richmond, contacts generally reported only slight-to-modest growth, with mixed consumer spending, soft/flat manufacturing, and ongoing CRE weakness. Wage growth and price pressures continued to ease, labor demand cooled somewhat with better labor supply, and lending conditions remained tight alongside weaker loan demand. Together with the SLOOS, this points to restrictive credit supply and softer demand acting as headwinds, reinforcing a cautious, higher-for-longer stance despite continued disinflation and a still-low unemployment rate. Net: tone shifts toward neutral.
